title: Invertibility of the explicit expression coefficient transpose
statement: Fix prime l, finite E/Q_l, D, o, and primitives d [def-sf-integral-expression-recursion-data]. Suppose rec: Reconstruction supplies reduction and limit closure and invertibility of the actual unit and counit on the specified constructible and Good domains. For every typed finite expression e with its geometric conditions and K in e.domain [def-sf-integral-system-expression-domain], the component transposeComparison(d,e)_K is an isomorphism. The associated canonicalComparisons is defined as the inverse of this explicit natural transformation; the inverse adjunction hom-set equivalence gives its whole-system coefficient identity. This statement asserts neither the unary/tensor recursion equations nor direct compactification agreement.

source.place: Coefficient-comparison sentence; agent-formulated expression-tree refinement, lem-sf-integral-expression-recursion, proof steps 1--11.

proof.text: Transport Good along a system isomorphism. Naturality transports normalization of the actual quotient transitions; evaluation isomorphisms preserve the same cohomological and Tor bounds, and finite-level constructibility is isomorphism invariant. Retain the origin levels, fixed and etale transitions, and origin squares; compose their evaluation isomorphisms with the evaluated system isomorphism. Naturality of the actual transition makes the new transition squares commute.

Strengthen expression induction to simultaneous constructibility of the integral value H and invertibility of the actual coefficientMap r: R H -> M. At a variable, constructibility is an input-domain hypothesis and r is the identity. For a unary node, transport Good of A M backward through A(r) to obtain Good of A R H. Reconstruction.reduction and the inductive constructibility hypothesis give the remaining basicUnaryDomain conditions at H itself. Reconstruction.limit and the supplied primitive isomorphism d_A identify the parent integral value with the constructible object L A R H; transport constructibility along this isomorphism. The primitive transpose equation identifies unaryReduction at H with R(d_A inverse) followed by the counit at A R H. Reconstruction.counit makes that counit invertible. Therefore unaryReduction and its composite with A(r), the parent coefficientMap, are invertible.

For tensor apply the preceding argument to the product of the two inductive coefficient isomorphisms. The tensor functor maps this product to an isomorphism, transporting Good of the tensor output back to the pair of reduced integral values. Reconstruction.reduction on both constructible child values gives basicTensorDomain. The supplied tensor primitive comparison and Reconstruction.limit give constructibility; tensorTranspose and Reconstruction.counit give invertibility of tensorReduction, and hence of the parent coefficientMap. The two induction hypotheses apply independently, including when variables repeat.

For compact support use the unary step for the open extension, using the intermediate open Good condition retained in the expression domain, and then for the proper image, using the root Good condition. The compactification scheme is finite type over the base by composition of its proper map with the finite-type root map. Finally transposeComparison is the unit at the now constructible integral value followed by L(coefficientMap), using coefficientTransformation_app. Reconstruction.unit makes the first factor invertible and functoriality makes the second invertible. The canonical inverse comparison and its coefficient identity remain the existing definitions and adjunction triangle calculation.

theorem transposeComparison_isIso (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u})
    (o : Operations l E) (d : Primitives l E D o) (rec : Reconstruction l E D)
    {I : Type u} {X : I → Over (Spec (.of D.k))}
    {W : Over (Spec (.of D.k))} (e : Expression _ I X W) (g : e.geometric)
    (K : (e.domain l E o).FullSubcategory) :
    IsIso ((transposeComparison l E d e g).app K)
